title: Console: route-level quantization profile toggle w/ compatibility warnings + impact preview
creator: Dylan Brooks
description:
Build Console UI controls to enable/disable Quantization Profiles per route (opt-in) and select a specific profile ref. UI must (1) preserve default behavior when unset/disabled, (2) surface deterministic compatibility warnings before save, and (3) provide a lightweight preview of expected cost/latency impact (best-effort; clearly labeled as estimates).

Scope (Console UI + Console backend integration):
- Route settings section: add “Quantization” card under Route → Runtime/Performance settings.
- Controls:
  - Enable toggle (default OFF): when OFF, quantization_profile_ref must resolve to “default/baseline”.
  - Profile selector (dropdown): list available profiles for the route’s model variant (and deployment context), with labels like “recommended”, “pinned version”, “experimental”.
  - Region/deployment tier constraints: show effective resolution context (region + tier) and if the route is multi-region, show per-region compatibility status.
- Compatibility + safety:
  - Call compatibility validation endpoint before save; block save on hard incompatibility.
  - Warn (non-blocking) on “soft constraints” (e.g., sequence length caveats, limited GPU SKU coverage) and require explicit confirmation.
  - Display fallback behavior: “If incompatible at runtime, Redwood will fall back to baseline precision; fallback events will be visible in metrics.”
  - Respect global kill-switch: if platform kill-switch is on, UI should show read-only state + banner (“Profiles disabled by platform policy”) and prevent edits.
- Impact preview:
  - Show estimated cost/token delta and p95 latency delta based on benchmark artifacts for that model/profile/GPU class (if available). If not available, show “No estimate available” + link to docs.
  - Preview must never imply guaranteed savings; copy should emphasize “estimate based on Redwood benchmarks; your workload may vary.”
- Audit + RBAC:
  - Only users with permission to edit routes (and new permission gate if required by policy) can change settings.
  - On save, write change with structured audit event; show link to change history view.

Out of scope:
- Automatic profile recommendation; auto-enablement.
- Deep per-prompt quality preview in Console (handled via eval harness playbook + external dashboards).

References:
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/prd-quantization-profile-library-opt-in.json
- ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0137-route-level-quantization-profile-enablement.json
- Console UX design: DES-418
- Control plane endpoints: see PR in flight (console backend endpoints + policy validation)

Acceptance Criteria:
1) A route owner can enable quantization for a route and select a profile; on save, the route config reflects quantization_profile_ref and enabled state.
2) When quantization is disabled, behavior is unchanged vs baseline; UI clearly indicates “Baseline precision (default)”.
3) Console blocks saving if profile is incompatible for the route context (model variant, deployment tier, region/GPU class) and displays actionable remediation.
4) Console surfaces non-blocking warnings (caveats) with confirm step in modal.
5) If global kill-switch is active, UI prevents edits and explains why.
6) Audit events are emitted and visible via change history (actor, timestamp, old/new values, route id).
7) Impact preview shows estimates when available and never claims guarantees; absence of data handled gracefully.
8) E2E tested: enable → observe applied/fallback in route details and links to metrics; disable → returns to baseline.

Implementation notes:
- Use Console backend endpoints added in PR-18496 for profile options + compatibility checks + write-through to control plane.
- Avoid thundering herd: cache profile options per model variant in Console backend and honor rate-limit headers.
- UI strings should align with docs wording (opt-in, rollback guidance, quality risks).
